basis: Choanal obstruction, deafness and septal defects define syndrome; lower eyelid coloboma in 12/14 supports ocular involvement. Renal anomalies are uncommon.
Central dopaminergic dysfunction causes rigidity, altered consciousness and autonomic dysfunction; rhabdomyolysis and kidney injury occur in only 5-29%.
Hereditary localized itching defines a cutaneous disorder; no evidence establishes another affected organ.
Developmental dentin and tooth-root abnormalities; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cardiomyopathy and ectodermal hair abnormalities define the syndrome; sparse hair occurs in 6/12. Motor delay alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Malignant vascular tumor arising within brain, spinal cord or meninges; endothelial histology does not establish separate cardiovascular involvement.
Intellectual disability, brain hypoplasia and seizures define the spectrum; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Joint hypermobility and skin fragility define the umbrella; severe arterial disease is concentrated in uncommon subtypes.
Brain abnormalities, intellectual disability and obesity define syndrome; supplied HPO reports night blindness in 80-99%, supporting ocular loss of function.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define disease; feeding difficulties, drooling and neurologic movement abnormalities do not establish other organ damage.
Airway ciliary dysfunction causes chronic respiratory disease; chronic middle-ear disease affects most PCD patients, although hearing impairment here is only 5-29%.
Primary malignant bone-forming tumor arising from the surface of long bones.
Benign multifocal glomus-cell proliferation associated with vascular spaces; no specific additional anatomical site is established.
Myopathy, cataract and cardiomyopathy are the defining manifestations across this spectrum; their combination varies by subtype.
Noninflammatory kidney pathology with protein loss; hypoalbuminemia and edema do not independently establish hepatic or cardiovascular disease.
Amino-acid handling disorder with hyperammonemia; neurologic impairment and malabsorption lack frequency estimates. Aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal damage.
Congenital peripheral hypomyelination; distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformity are typical (>30%). Respiratory dysfunction frequency is unspecified.
Carcinoma originates in the stomach; salivary-gland type describes its histology.
Epileptic encephalopathy and pituitary insufficiency define disease; retinal dystrophy occurs in only 1/7, and nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Dysplastic cerebellar lesion causes neurologic dysfunction; associated thyroid, skin and other tumors are separate disorders, often reflecting an underlying PTEN syndrome.
Breast inflammation has no anatomical axis; this umbrella includes sterile obstructive mastitis, so an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not required.
Ovarian epithelial tumor involves a reproductive organ; mucinous histology does not establish gastrointestinal origin or endocrine dysfunction.
Immune and blood-cell defects with ocular albinism define CHS; progressive neurologic dysfunction affects most long-term survivors. Skin, hepatic and periodontal findings omitted by cap.
Hereditary lens opacities cause progressive loss of visual acuity.
Chronic inflammatory papules and plaques involve skin; lymphoma progression is a later risk, and the umbrella does not establish a specific immune mechanism.
